args.title: Triage issue 4410
args.body:
File: src/config.ts

The configuration parser `int` in `src/config.ts` uses `Number.parseInt(raw, 10)` to parse integer environment variables such as `TOKEN_TTL_ENVS` and `RESET_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES`. When passed a string like `"12h"`, `Number.parseInt("12h", 10)` parses leading digits (`12`) and successfully returns `12` without throwing an error or complaining, leading to unexpected behavior as noted in the issue and discussion (where maintainer priya-s confirms: 'Even so, a value like 12h should stop the service from starting rather than be read as 12').

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

In src/api/health.ts, the readiness health check endpoint (GET /api/v1/health) computes the HTTP status code as `res.status(status === "down" ? 503 : 200)`. When the queue is degraded (queueDepth > 500) but the database is up, `status` is "degraded", resulting in an HTTP 200 response instead of a non-200 status code. The issue asks how load balancer probes should treat this. The behavior is implemented as designed per health.ts and docs/API.md ("503 when the database is down"), making this a question about how the health check and load balancer probes work.

args.title: Triage issue 4423
args.body:
File: src/i18n/index.ts

src/i18n/index.ts parses the Accept-Language header by splitting on comma and taking the first supported language, ignoring quality values (q parameters). As described in issue #4423, headers like `en;q=0.3, fr-FR;q=0.9` are parsed incorrectly because English appears first despite having a lower quality weight.
